title: SGP joint pricing with a shared game-environment factor

title: Team props and to-score-first from a drive-level Poisson race
summary: Team props are modeled as home ~ N((T+S)/2, sigma_team = 11.5) and away ~ N((T-S)/2, sigma_team), with sigma_team below sigma_margin/sqrt(2) to encode score correlation. To-score-first comes from a drive-level Poisson race: P(home first) = lambda_h/(lambda_h + lambda_a) plus a possession edge of about 4 percent. These are the free first-scoring and team-total markets that flat models misprice.

title: Keener matrix must be column-normalized (row-norm trap)

title: Simultaneous Kelly needs backtracking line search; correlation tax emerges

title: Brier Murphy decomposition with uncertainty as the variance floor

Would change: reports distinguish miscalibration from no-skill, so an engine cannot hide a useless model behind a good-looking Brier.

title: Context engine geo-coded features and the closing-spread-prices-context finding
summary: context_engine.py geo-codes 7,341 games (haversine travel, timezone, altitude, rest, dome) plus 91 referees. The doctrine finding is that the closing spread already prices context: rest/travel/tz are not significant versus close while travel is +0.4 pts per 1000mi (t=2.14), so context edges exist only versus EARLY lines. Post-bye road teams are -2.33 pts (t=-2.54), division games -0.96 (t=-2.44), SNF +1.69 (t=1.85, marginal), and referee environments carry an EB signal sd of 1.09 pts (Carey -1.75 to Smith +1.46).

title: Pick6/PrizePicks structural holds 25-40.6% and correlation transfer rho=0.30 hold 0, rho=0.50 player +26%
summary: Payout-table engines decoded for Pick6/PrizePicks: structural holds of 25-40.6% at fair legs with breakeven p/leg 0.545-0.585 versus their engineered ~50% lines; Flex 5/6 tables are player-+EV at a fair 50%, which is why legs get shaded to 52% and above; and correlation transfer where rho=0.30 gives operator hold 0 and rho=0.50 gives the player +26%, which explains why same-game stacks get capped. title: Production aging curves: AV per game by years-in-league for QB/RB/WR/TE
summary: Own computation over 28,617 player-seasons from 1999-2026 rosters with a sample floor of n>=25 per position-year gives AV/game by years-in-league: QB 0.471 at year 0 rising to 0.610 at year 5 and 0.699 at year 8; RB 0.361 at year 0, peak 0.434 in years 2-3, then 0.406 by year 8; WR 0.237 at year 0 climbing straight to 0.391 by year 7; TE 0.100 at year 0. Read-outs called weapons: the RB cliff is measurable, rookie WRs produce 60 percent of their year-7 value, rookie TEs are nearly unusable at 0.100 which is 22 percent of year 4, and the QB sophomore dip is visible at 0.577 to 0.560/0.554.

title: Hawkes self-exciting scoring process with home/away excitation asymmetry
summary: Named equation: multivariate Hawkes intensity lambda_c(t) = mu_c + sum over c' and t_i<t of alpha_cc' * exp(-beta_cc'(t - t_i)), with mu_c the base scoring rate per event type (TD, FG, safety) and alpha the excitation of c' on c, requiring branching ratio n = sum(alpha)/beta < 1 for stationarity; fitted by MLE on play timestamps. The football weighting invention is drive-level events with possession flips and separate home/away alpha estimates to define momentum asymmetry, feeding a state-dependent drift into the live repricing drift term. Verified unclaimed on arXiv (2 hits, both soccer). Kill test: out-of-sample log-loss of next-score-time predictions versus a constant-rate Poisson baseline AND versus the live close's implied drift; win feeds live repricing only. Data READY post PBP re-download.

title: MaxEnt inverse reinforcement learning to recover coach reward weights (irrationality index)
summary: MaxEnt IRL (Ziebart 2008) recovers reward weights theta such that pi_coach(a|s) = exp(theta^T phi(s,a)) / sum over a' of exp(theta^T phi(s,a')), with phi = [delta WP, variance, time-cost, score-margin], estimated by theta* = argmax sum of log pi(a_i|s_i; theta) on coach trajectories. The football weighting adds our own win probability function plus situational features, and the learned gap between theta_coach and theta_WP defines a coach irrationality index. Angle: live WP pricing when an irrational-policy coach faces 4th-and-short, plus totals drift on hot-seat coaches. Kill test: predict next-season coach decisions better than nfl4th recommendations AND better than market-implied, then simulate the WP cost.

title: EVT prop tails: GEV/GPD for longest-X markets where the book assumes Gaussian
summary: Peaks-over-threshold EVT: P(max <= x) approximately exp(-[1 + xi(x-u)/sigma]^(-1/xi)) (GEV) or GPD for exceedances over u, fitted to player-season distributions of maximum play length such as longest rush, reception or completion. The doc's key argument is that book pricing of longest-X props uses rough Normal quantiles (DK's ladder recon shows the whole curve is Gaussian-fit) while maxima are not Gaussian, so the book's shape assumption is wrong for tail markets and the mispricing is systematic. Registry's own priority order ranks this first today. Kill test: backtest 2023-25 longest-X props with Brier/log-loss for GPD versus book-implied versus Normal. Data READY post PBP re-pull with the DK ladders in hand.

title: GAS score-driven team strength with fat-tailed innovations (drop-in Kalman upgrade)
summary: GAS(p,q) from Creal-Koopman-Lucas 2013: theta_t = omega + A*s_{t-1} + B*theta_{t-1} where the score s_t = d log L(y_t|theta_t)/d theta_t, so the model updates strength by the likelihood score of the surprise, with t-distributed innovations y_t ~ t_nu(mu_team(t), sigma^2) handling blowouts without ad-hoc variance floors. It replaces or augments kalman_ratings so a 30-point loss moves ratings more than Gaussian Kalman would. Kill test: walk-forward CRPS versus Kalman AND versus the Gaussian-close baseline whose bar is CRPS 7.109; adoption only if the bar is beaten.

title: Synthetic control for single-team regime events (QB injury, OC firing, trade)
summary: Synthetic control treatment effect ATT = (y_1^T - sum_j w_j y_j^T) where w solves min ||y_1^pre - sum_j w_j y_j^pre||^2 subject to w >= 0 and sum w = 1, building a weighted placebo twin of team i from other teams' trajectories. The football weighting sets the unit as team-week and the outcome as market-adjusted EPA/margin/total residuals with a donor pool of 31 teams times lags, targeting event-study edge windows where the market takes 1-2 weeks to re-price regime changes. Kill test: placebo-in-time fake event dates must show no effect, plus a pre-period fit RMSE floor.

Kill test: do shape features add predictive power on rookie EPA beyond speed, acceleration and draft capital, walk-forward by draft class.

title: Double machine learning for context factors: debiased rest/travel/short-week/turf coefficients
summary: Chernozhukov et al 2018 double ML: cross-fit nuisance models m(X) and g(X), then theta_hat = sum (Y - g(X))(T - m(X)) / sum (T - m(X))^2, giving Neyman-orthogonal estimates so ML nuisance error does not bias theta. The football weighting sets T as the context factor (post-bye, travel direction, turf), Y as the market-adjusted residual of margin minus close, and X as team strength lags and schedule features, replacing pooled OLS which absorbed strength confounds. This is described as wish #9 done rigorously. Kill test: coefficient stability across folds plus placebo treatments where random fake rest weeks must yield approximately zero.

title: Conformal drift gate: MMD two-sample test that widens the abstain floor on non-exchangeable weeks
summary: Two-sample MMD^2 with kernel k between this week's feature distribution and the calibration window: MMD^2 = 1/m^2 sum sum k(x_i,x_j) + 1/n^2 sum sum k(y_i,y_j) - 2/(mn) sum sum k(x_i,y_j), with a permutation-test p-value; if MMD^2 exceeds its null quantile the week is not exchangeable with calibration and the abstain floor widens. It ties to the non-exchangeable conformal family in the brain doc and the abstain wish. Kill test: does the gate improve net CLV by skipping flagged weeks versus betting all weeks; data is team-state features weekly and READY.

title: PP margin-curve kill-shot spec: 4-step p_model and EV derivation
summary: Method spec: (1) over-only PP lines vs DK-reconstructed (mu_hat, sigma_hat) -> p_model = 1 - Phi((line - mu)/sigma); (2) slip EV(n, mode) = prod(p_i)*M - 1 for Power or sum over outcome tiers for Flex under independence; (3) per-stat margin curve as EV vs number of legs using each stat's mean p at PP over-only depth (about -0.85 sigma average); (4) compare per-leg breakeven 54-57.7% against our p at their posted over-only lines to find pockets where prod(p)*M > 1.

title: Information-theoretic edge decomposition block
summary: Four coupled quantities define edge: information gap D_KL(P_true || P_market) is the theoretical maximum edge the market leaves on the table; model information I(P_model; Y) = H(Y) - H(Y | P_model); per-bet edge E[Profit] = P_true * (Odds - 1) - (1 - P_true); and information ratio IR = I(P_model; Y) / D_KL(P_true || P_market) which normalizes extracted edge by available edge. A model with zero mutual information about outcomes cannot be profitable regardless of staking.

title: Independence fallacy in Same Game Parlays
summary: Naive SGP pricing multiplies leg probabilities P(Leg1) x P(Leg2), e.g. Team A covers -7.5 and Team A RB1 over 85.5 rushing yards. These legs are positively correlated because covering a large spread often happens through rushing control, so the true joint probability exceeds the product and the naive product systematically underprices the parlay. Copula-based joint estimation consistently beats the independence assumption for SGP and correlated-leg pricing.

title: Narrativization trap and zero-signal sports prose
summary: Sports commentary prose (e.g. 'the Chiefs will cover because Mahomes is playing at an MVP level') is post-hoc rationalization carrying zero predictive signal and produces negative expected value when evaluated against closing lines. LLMs trained on news text exhibit systematic overconfidence and narrative bias. The operational implication is that explanation text must never be treated as evidence and reasoning traces must be scored on computation, not fluency.

title: Sklar's theorem copula decomposition
summary: For any joint CDF H(x1,...,xd) with marginals F1(x1),...,Fd(xd) there exists a copula C: [0,1]^d -> [0,1] such that H(x1,...,xd) = C(F1(x1),...,Fd(xd)); conversely any copula with those marginals yields a valid joint distribution. This separates marginal modelling (individual player performance) from dependence structure (how performances correlate), which is exactly what correlated-leg and SGP pricing needs.

title: Frank copula closed form with dependence sign
summary: C_theta(u,v) = -(1/theta) * ln( 1 + ((e^{-theta u} - 1)(e^{-theta v} - 1)) / (e^{-theta} - 1) ). As theta -> 0 it converges to the independence copula C(u,v) = uv; theta > 0 gives positive dependence and theta < 0 negative dependence. Documented applications: football match outcomes (goals by each team), tennis first-serve performance, baseball batting partnerships. The Student t-copula with 5 degrees of freedom is noted as a strong alternative for tail dependence.

For sports data with limited samples the Inference Function for Margins (IFM) two-step method is preferred: estimate marginal parameters first, then plug the marginals in and estimate theta.

title: Frechet-Hoeffding bounds as deterministic joint-probability gate
summary: Any valid copula satisfies W(u,v) = max(0, u+v-1) <= C(u,v) <= min(u,v) = M(u,v); equivalently for events A, B with probabilities p_A, p_B: max(0, p_A + p_B - 1) <= P(A and B) <= min(p_A, p_B). The verification layer applies this as a hard check: any reasoning trace reporting a joint probability outside the bounds receives an immediate terminal penalty. The evaluation table lists copula compliance at 100 percent with baseline models violating bounds in 40 percent of cases.

title: KL divergence as market-inefficiency ceiling
summary: D_KL(P || Q) = sum_x P(x) log( P(x) / Q(x) ). In betting, D_KL(P_true || P_market) measures how much information the market lacks and therefore the theoretical maximum edge available on that market. Any signal whose mutual information with outcomes approaches zero cannot be monetized no matter how the staking is tuned.

title: Mutual information and binary entropy signal screen
summary: Signal value measured as I(X;Y) = sum_{x,y} P(x,y) log( P(x,y) / (P(x) P(y)) ), which for binary outcomes reduces to I(X;Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X) with H(Y) = -p log p - (1-p) log(1-p). This gives a model-free screen that ranks candidate features by how many outcome bits they carry, independent of any predictive model.

Applied to betting, it measures how much information line movements carry about future outcomes beyond the outcome series' own history, i.e. a principled steam-detection statistic.

title: Baseball 24-state base-out Markov chain run expectancy

The 24-state base-out chain enumerates base configurations 000, 100, 020, 003, 120, 103, 023, 123 crossed with outs 0, 1, 2, with transitions Single, Double, Triple, Home Run, Walk, Out, Strikeout; P_ij is the probability of transitioning from state i to state j on a plate appearance. Run expectancy is computed from this transition matrix and is the standard baseline since Bukiet et al. (1997).

title: Continuous-time MDP value recursion and HJB condition
summary: In-game decision making uses V(s,t) = max_{a in A} { r(s,a) + lambda * integral_t^{t+Delta} E[V(s',t') | s,a] dt' }, with immediate reward r(s,a), discount rate lambda and next state s'. The Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman optimality condition is dV/dt + max_a { r(s,a) + sum_{s'} lambda(s'|s,a)[V(s',t) - V(s,t)] } = 0. Research grounding: continuous-time within-play valuation in the NFL using player tracking data with LSTM play-outcome models feeding expected points and win probability.

title: Kelly criterion optimal fraction and growth rate
summary: For win probability p and net odds b (win b units per 1 staked): f* = (b p - (1-p)) / b = (p(b+1) - 1) / b. This maximizes the expected log growth rate g(f) = p ln(1 + f b) + (1-p) ln(1 - f). Note the Kelly fraction is zero when p(b+1) <= 1, i.e. the bet is not +EV.

title: Multi-asset Kelly for correlated simultaneous bets
summary: For simultaneous correlated wagers the objective is f* = argmax_f E[ln(1 + f^T R)] and the solution is f* = Sigma^{-1} mu, with mu the vector of expected excess returns and Sigma the covariance matrix of returns. Correlated legs must therefore be staked jointly rather than independently, and Sigma must come from the same copula/correlation estimates used for parlay pricing.

title: Fractional Kelly safety scaling

Research on phase transitions in optimal betting shows fractional Kelly gives a better trade-off between growth rate and risk of ruin under parameter uncertainty.

title: Brier score definition and Murphy binning formulas
summary: BS = (1/N) sum_{i=1..N} (f_i - o_i)^2 with forecast f_i and binary outcome o_i. Murphy decomposition with K bins: BS = Reliability - Resolution + Uncertainty, Reliability = (1/N) sum_{k=1..K} n_k (f_k - o_bar_k)^2, Resolution = (1/N) sum_{k=1..K} n_k (o_bar_k - o_bar)^2, Uncertainty = o_bar(1 - o_bar). Lower reliability is better (0 = perfectly calibrated); higher resolution is better (0 = always predicting base rate); uncertainty is irreducible and depends only on base rate. Brier is a strictly proper scoring rule, so it is minimized in expectation only by reporting true beliefs.

title: Expected Calibration Error (ECE) binning metric
summary: ECE = sum_{m=1..M} (|B_m| / N) * |acc(B_m) - conf(B_m)| over M confidence bins, where B_m is the set of predictions in bin m, acc is realized accuracy and conf the average confidence. Documented research findings: a persistent discrimination (AUROC) vs calibration (ECE) trade-off, structurally-aware models achieve the best ECE, and calibration drift under reasoning occurs because long chain-of-thought yields internally consistent but factually wrong trajectories that end in overconfidence. Evaluation table target is ECE < 0.03 with 10 bins against a human-expert 0.05 baseline.

title: CRPS for continuous prop outcomes and Gaussian closed form
summary: CRPS(F, y) = integral from -inf to +inf of (F(t) - I(t >= y))^2 dt scores a full predictive CDF F against observation y. For a Gaussian predictive distribution N(mu, sigma^2) it has the closed form CRPS = sigma * [ z(2 Phi(z) - 1) + 2 phi(z) - 1/sqrt(pi) ] with z = (y - mu)/sigma, Phi the standard normal CDF and phi the standard normal PDF. This is the correct scoring rule for continuous prop lines such as rushing yards rather than a Brier score on a thresholded event.

title: Process Reward Model step score and Bellman trajectory value
summary: A PRM scores each reasoning step r_t = P_psi(c_t = 1 | s_t, a_t) over trajectory tau = (s_0, a_0, s_1, a_1, ..., s_T), where c_t in {0,1} marks step correctness. The global trajectory value follows the Bellman-style recursion Q*(s_t, a_t) = E_{tau_{t+1:T} ~ pi}[ product_{i=t..T} I(c_i = 1) | s_t, a_t ]. Named architectures cited: PathFinder-PRM (2025) hierarchical error-aware discriminative PRM reaching PRMScore 67.7 versus prior 65.5 with 3x less data; GroundedPRM (2025) tree-guided fidelity-aware PRM; Med-PRM retrieval-augmented PRM verifying each step against knowledge bases, relevant for injury reports and historical data.

title: Adversarial invariance tests: entity swap, temporal shuffle, structural perturbation
summary: Entity swapping: replace all proper nouns with synthetic entities (Team Alpha, Player 1, Date X) while keeping statistics and structure identical; if the output shifts by more than epsilon = 0.02 the model is relying on memorized text rather than reasoning. Temporal shuffling: permute the time ordering while preserving all other information; a genuine temporal reasoner produces different but mathematically consistent outputs, a memorizer reproduces the original. Structural perturbation: change team names, dates, venue names and weather by small amounts; wild swings in conclusions indicate non-causal computation.

title: Copula parameter consistency tolerance 0.005
summary: When the model reports a copula parameter theta_hat it must satisfy P(A and B) = C_theta_hat(p_A, p_B) within |P_reported - C_theta_hat(p_A, p_B)| < epsilon with epsilon = 0.005 (half a percent). This binds the reported joint probability to the reported dependence parameter so a trace cannot quote an attractive parlay price while quoting an inconsistent copula.

title: Temporal Fusion Transformer for multi-horizon sports forecasting
summary: TFT ingests time-series features [x_1..x_T], static covariates s (team identity, venue) and known future inputs [k_1..k_T], runs a Variable Selection Network, static covariate encoders, an LSTM encoder plus interpretable multi-head attention with gating layers, and emits quantile outputs P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 as a full predictive distribution. It handles multiple horizons (quarter, half, game, season) and provides interpretable attention weights. Cited successes: MLB pitcher ERA prediction beating RNN baselines and existing projection systems, and football result prediction for goals, corners and cards.

title: GRPO group-relative advantage normalized by median and MAD

title: Backward verifier error correction inverts the noise transition matrix
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 1, backward correction; and Python RLVR_GRPO_Engine)
summary: Backward correction algebraically inverts the verifier noise transition matrix to recover an unbiased surrogate of the clean reward: R_backward = (Rtilde - rho_0) / (1 - rho_0 - rho_1). Caller supplies observed rewards and the two noise rates; returns a debiased reward used in the policy-gradient estimator. Fail-closed condition: if rho_0 + rho_1 >= 1.0 the noise rates exceed the informational capacity of the channel and the implemented routine returns an all-zero reward tensor instead of a meaningless division.

title: Forward verifier error correction reweights the objective without amplifying variance
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 1, forward correction)
summary: Forward correction is the complementary verifier-noise treatment: instead of transforming rewards, it modifies the optimization objective, reweighting the probability distributions associated with policy updates so that the expected update direction aligns with the clean gradient. The document's claimed property is that this stays highly stable even under heavy verifier noise, without the sampling-variance amplification that reward inversion can cause. Reported symptom it resolves: delayed learning curves and plateau states in naive RLVR runs.

title: PRM error taxonomy: arithmetic, logical, factual, omission, consistency
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 1, Step-Wise Process Reward Modeling table)
summary: The hierarchical PRM discriminator classifies intermediate reasoning nodes across five discrete error topologies with sports-context examples: Arithmetic = violation of algebraic operations or numerical precision (e.g. computing 0.5 x 0.3 = 0.20 instead of 0.15 during correlation); Logical = invalid deduction or violation of probabilistic axioms (assuming independence when structural correlation exists); Factual = integration of statistically false or ungrounded priors (wrong historical closing-line-value offset); Omission = failure to account for required causal covariates (projecting passing volume without adjusting for terminal wind velocity); Consistency = internal contradiction across reasoning sub-graphs (conflicting probabilities for identical events in different nodes). This gives the step scorer a labeled failure taxonomy rather than a binary pass/fail.

title: Bellman Q-decay as a multiplicative trajectory product of step validities
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 1, Bellman constraints; GroundedPRM / PathFinder prior art)
summary: True trajectory value under the monotonic Bellman Q-decay constraint: Q*(s_t,a_t) = E_{tau_{t+1:T} ~ pi}[ prod_{i=t..T} I(c_i = 1) | s_t, a_t ], where the PRM emits a discrete correctness scalar c_t in {0,1} per step. Because the product is multiplicative, any single ungrounded assertion or invalid algebraic step forces c_t = 0 and every downstream Q* to exactly 0 regardless of terminal alignment, so early logical fatal errors cannot be preserved by a lucky final answer. Cited prior art: GroundedPRM and PathFinder, which separate structural reasoning validity from arithmetic accuracy to improve PRMScore.

title: Frank copula closed-form CDF with independence limit at theta to 0
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 2, Archimedean and Vine Copula Formulations)
summary: Closed-form Frank copula for uniform marginals u,v in [0,1]: C_theta(u,v) = -(1/theta) ln(1 + ((e^{-theta u} - 1)(e^{-theta v} - 1)) / (e^{-theta} - 1)), with parameter theta in R excluding 0 driving strength and direction of dependence and converging to the independence copula as theta to 0. The document's stated reason for making Frank the core bivariate structure is that it accommodates both positive and negative dependence across the whole unit square, unlike one-sided families.

title: Archimedean family selection rule: Clayton for lower tail, Gumbel for upper tail, Frank for symmetric
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 2, family comparison)
summary: Family-selection guidance for sports dependence: Frank copula as the symmetric core structure; Clayton copula exhibits strict lower-tail dependence, which maps to blowout game scripts and injury truncations; Gumbel copula enforces upper-tail dependence, which maps to shootout or overtime scenarios. The operational implication is that a single-family copula engine cannot represent both blowout and overtime dependence, so tail-relevant markets (NRFI/YRFI-style derivatives, overtime props) require asymmetric families.

title: Documented defect: copula verifier uses scalar Brent on Frank only, omitting Clayton and Gumbel families

title: R-vine and C-vine hierarchical copula decomposition for multi-leg parlays
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 2, vine copula formulation)
summary: To model three-or-more-variable correlated structures such as Same Game Parlays, the architecture decomposes the d-dimensional joint density into marginals and a cascade of conditional bivariate copulas: f(x_1..x_d) = prod_{k=1..d} f_k(x_k) * prod_{i=1..d-1} prod_{e in E_i} c_{C_{e,a}, C_{e,b} | D_e}( F(x_{C_{e,a}} | x_{D_e}), F(x_{C_{e,b}} | x_{D_e}) ). Sklar's theorem guarantees the decomposition exists; the practical gain is that each edge of the R-vine tree can carry its own parametric copula family, so heterogeneous dependence (symmetric in one pair, tail-asymmetric in another) is representable. Regular Vine and Canonical Vine constructions are both named.

title: Frechet-Hoeffding bounds as a fail-closed reasoning kill trigger
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 2, Frechet-Hoeffding Invariants)
summary: For any two events with uniform marginals u and v the joint probability must satisfy max(0, u+v-1) <= C(u,v) <= min(u,v). The document elevates this from a check to a kill trigger: if a neural reasoning trajectory estimates a joint probability outside the bounds, the inference path has suffered a mathematical hallucination, the reasoning step is flagged c_t = 0, the trajectory is terminated and the inference discarded. Implemented check in the listing: verify_frechet_hoeffding_bounds returns False when joint_prob exceeds upper_bound + 1e-6.

title: Split conformal non-conformity quantile with finite-sample correction
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 2, Distribution-Free Split Conformal Prediction)
summary: The audit explicitly reinstates the conformal algorithm the (2) pass abandoned as non-executable: for desired marginal coverage 1-alpha the non-conformity threshold is q_hat = Quantile_{1-alpha}( { |y_i - mu_hat(x_i)| : i in I_cal } , ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)) / n ), computed with the 'higher' interpolation convention. title: CQR and SPCI for serially dependent sports schedules
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 2, conformal variants)
summary: The architecture pairs Conformalized Quantile Regression with Sequential Predictive Conformal Inference because NFL and NBA seasons are ordered, serially dependent time series rather than exchangeable draws. SPCI adaptively recalibrates the non-conformity threshold using localized residual autocorrelations, dynamically tightening or expanding prediction bands in response to structural meta-shifts or mid-season regime changes. Underlying rationale: linear quantile regression suffers under-coverage bias in finite samples and fails to capture the variance of continuous player props.

title: Murphy partition explicit bin formulas for reliability, resolution and uncertainty
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 3, Murphy Vector Partition table)
summary: Explicit bin-level definitions over K probability bins containing n_k forecasts out of population N, with base rate o_bar: Reliability REL = (1/N) sum_{k=1..K} n_k (f_k - o_bar_k)^2 measuring calibration deviation between forecast probabilities and empirical outcomes (perfect calibration gives REL=0); Resolution RES = (1/N) sum_{k=1..K} n_k (o_bar_k - o_bar)^2 quantifying the ability to discern outcomes deviating from the baseline average; Uncertainty UNC = o_bar(1 - o_bar), the irreducible variance of the event base rate and the theoretical predictability ceiling. BS = REL - RES + UNC.

title: REL greater than UNC as a quarantine kill trigger for degenerate forecasters
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 3, Fail-Closed Kill Trigger)
summary: Operational boundary derived from the partition: a forecaster that indiscriminately predicts the global base rate achieves REL=0 and RES=0, giving BS exactly equal to UNC. Therefore REL > UNC means the engine is operating mathematically worse than a naive climatological average; when this condition is breached the pipeline triggers an immediate execution halt and quarantines the model until structural recalibration occurs. Implemented in ProbabilisticScoringEngine.murphy_brier_decomposition as a raised ValueError ('Fatal Calibration Error: REL > UNC. Model performance is degenerate.').

title: CRPS Gaussian closed form with normal CDF and PDF terms
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 3, CRPS)
summary: For a Gaussian predictive distribution N(mu, sigma^2), CRPS = sigma * [ z(2 Phi(z) - 1) + 2 phi(z) - 1/sqrt(pi) ] with z = (y - mu)/sigma, y the realized ground truth, Phi the standard normal CDF and phi the standard normal PDF. The document notes that scoring probability mass at a scalar threshold is insufficient for continuous props such as rushing yards or total points, and that extreme heavy-tailed metrics require non-Gaussian mixture formulations instead of this closed form.

title: 24-state base-out Markov chain with pitcher-fatigue and umpire-bias conditioning
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 4, 24-State Base-Out Markov Chains)
summary: MLB half-inning progression is a finite Markov chain over 24 transient states formed by the cross-product of 8 runner occupancies (bases empty 000 through bases loaded 123) and 3 out states (0,1,2), with transition probability matrix P in R^{24x24} governing state-to-state movement after each plate appearance. Key operational additions beyond the static chain: the matrices are dynamically conditioned on pitcher fatigue vectors, specifically Times Through the Order degradation penalties, and on localized umpire strike-zone bias profiles. For NRFI/YRFI derivative markets the engine computes the exact absorbing-state probability vector, isolating transition paths reaching the 3-out absorbing state while verifying cumulative run generation across the path equals exactly zero.

title: CTMDP state evolution SDE and Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman optimal control for win probability added
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 4, CTMDPs and HJB Formulations)
summary: Football and basketball are modeled as continuous-time Markov decision processes whose latent state (clock, accumulated fatigue, spatial positioning) evolves as ds = f(s,a,theta) dt + sigma dW(t), with drift f(s,a,theta) and Wiener noise sigma dW(t). In-game decisions such as a fourth-down conversion attempt or late-game clock management are cast as optimal control: the value function V(s,t) mapping state to maximal expected win probability solves the HJB PDE dV/dt + max_a { r(s,a) + grad V . f(s,a,theta) + (1/2) Tr( sigma sigma^T grad^2 V ) } = 0. The document states the architecture approximates the HJB solution by deep value iteration to produce real-time win probability added metrics.

title: Prospect theory parameter bounds as hard kill conditions
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 4, Behavioral Decision Modeling)
summary: Piecewise power-law value function v(x) = x^alpha for x >= 0 and -lambda(-x)^beta for x < 0, defined over deviations from a subjective reference point rather than absolute wealth. The document converts the parameterization into enforced bounds: lambda >= 1.0 encodes loss aversion and alpha, beta <= 1.0 encode diminishing sensitivity. Any programmatic estimate or reasoning trace implying alpha > 1.0 (convex utility on gains) or lambda < 1.0 triggers immediate system termination because it violates foundational axioms and invalidates the behavioral model.

title: Shin de-biasing: extracting true probabilities from decimal odds via the insider proportion
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 5, Shin's De-Biasing and Asymmetric Insider Trading)
summary: Shin (1991, 1992, 1993) models a monopolist bookmaker facing an unknown proportion z of insider traders who hold perfect future knowledge and wager only on the guaranteed winner, which is the mechanism behind the favorite-longshot bias. As operationalized in the Jullien and Salanie (1994) extension, with normalized inverse odds pi_i = 1/O_i from decimal odds O_i, the true objective probability is p_i = [ sqrt( z^2 + 4(1-z) pi_i^2 ) - z ] / [ 2(1-z) ]. The latent insider parameter z is recovered numerically by constrained root finding (Brent's method) bounded in [0,1) subject to the constraint that the extracted true probabilities sum to exactly 1.0. This replaces naive proportional de-vig, which fails because bookmakers do not distribute margin uniformly.

title: Shin probability extraction routine with fail-closed non-convergence branch
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 5, Python listing)
summary: MarketMicrostructureEngine.shin_probability_extraction(decimal_odds) computes implied_probs = 1/decimal_odds, defines the scalar objective_z(z) = sum(true_p) - 1 with a 1e9 penalty when z is outside [0,1), solves z_opt = brentq(objective_z, 0.0, 0.999), then returns (term - z_opt) / (2(1 - z_opt)) where term = sqrt(z_opt^2 + 4(1 - z_opt) implied_probs^2). A ValueError from the solver is caught and re-raised as 'Shin optimization failed to converge. Market data is corrupt.', so degenerate odds cannot silently produce probabilities. The 0.999 upper bound is the copyable constant.

title: Constrained multi-asset Kelly with covariance and conformal-derived uncertainty discounts
source_file: Deep Research Equation Extraction (3).docx (section MODULE 5, Multi-Asset Correlated Kelly Criterion)
summary: Optimal staking vector f* = argmax_f E[ ln(1 + f^T R) ] subject to the exposure boundary sum_i f_i <= f_max, solved as a constrained convex optimization. The objective directly incorporates the cross-market covariance matrix Sigma so that correlated simultaneous wagers do not double-count edge; scalar Kelly on correlated legs is stated to produce catastrophic over-leverage and ruin. Additional risk control: the optimizer iteratively penalizes the objective vector with parameter-uncertainty discounts computed proportionally to the residual variance observed in the distribution-free split conformal bounds.

title: Disagreement 3: rules-aware generative likelihoods beat generic ML classification heads
summary: Fitting generic black-box classifiers such as XGBoost or generic neural nets directly to binary win/loss labels discards structural domain information. Paper 1607.00379 similarly models rugby with a log-linear Poisson likelihood over attack, defense and home advantage.

title: Contradiction 1: raw quantile regression under-covers; must be conformalized
summary: Lin, Trivedi and Sun 2021 (arXiv:2106.05515) prove linear quantile regression has an inherent under-coverage bias: for alpha > 0.5 and small d/n, the learned alpha-quantile achieves coverage of roughly alpha - (alpha - 0.5) * d/n regardless of the noise distribution. Romano, Patterson and Candes 2019 (arXiv:1905.03222) fix this with Conformalized Quantile Regression using conformity score E_i = max(q_alpha_lo(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_alpha_hi(X_i)), guaranteeing finite-sample P(Y in C) >= 1 - alpha under exchangeability. Raw quantile outputs from nets or boosted trees must be treated as uncalibrated proposal distributions and passed through a conformal step.

priority_reason: Numeric line coverage is currently unguaranteed without this step.

title: Contradiction 2: fail-closed refusal vs quantile clamping (fake tightness)
summary: Angelopoulos and Bates 2021 (arXiv:2107.07511) and Dietterich and Hostetler (2206.04860) specify q_hat as the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n empirical quantile of calibration scores, requiring delta >= 1/(n+1). When n is too small, distribution-free coverage cannot be guaranteed without emitting infinite intervals or abstaining. Clamping quantiles to empirical maximums when n < ceil(1/alpha) - 1 violates the coverage proof and produces under-coverage and fake tightness. The audit mandates a fail-closed No-Bet or abstention decision in those cases.

priority_reason: Directly prevents betting on falsely tight intervals in small samples.

title: Contradiction 3: binary point probabilities need Venn-Abers multiprobability bounds
summary: Barber, Candes, Ramdas and Tibshirani 2020 prove that in binary regression any algorithm giving distribution-free coverage of the conditional label probability pi(X) must also cover the binary label Y, so meaningful bounded-length distribution-free intervals for pi(X) are impossible without structural assumptions. Van der Laan and Alaa 2025 (arXiv:2502.05676) propose Generalized Venn-Abers calibration producing valid multiprobability bounds [p0, p1] containing the true conditional probability in finite samples under exchangeability. GSE should output [p0, p1] for side probabilities and use the interval width (p1 - p0) as an epistemic uncertainty measure for EV calculations and selective gating.

title: Production confidence inversion: 80%+ confidence wins only 37.5% of the time
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf

title: Global isotonic regression and temperature scaling cause minority collapse
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: The current architecture applies global isotonic regression plus temperature scaling, which minimizes global Expected Calibration Error but triggers minority collapse. Pooling heterogeneous regimes (heavily juiced favorites, volatile longshots, distinct weather paradigms) into one calibration curve artificially suppresses the variance of minority subpopulations to satisfy a macro-level objective. The audit calls the confidence inversion a textbook consequence of marginal-over-conditional calibration.

title: Adopt Conformal Risk Control bounding expected loss, not just miscoverage
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: Conformal Risk Control (Angelopoulos, Bates and colleagues) extends conformal methods beyond miscoverage to bound the expected value of any monotonically decreasing loss function. title: Sarmanov mixing kernel captures negative dependence missed by bivariate Poisson
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: Traditional bivariate Poisson constructions generate dependence through a shared latent variable, which mathematically restricts correlation to non-negative values. That regime is structurally unpriced today.

title: Random-memory Hawkes process with a multivariate excite-inhibit transition matrix
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: The engine should implement Hawkes processes to model momentum and self-excitation in high-tempo sequences. A random-memory Hawkes process treats the duration of self-excitation as a random variable rather than an infinite-memory exponential decay, capturing scoring bursts and turnover cascades. It requires a multivariate excite-and-inhibit transition matrix so a successful offensive play raises subsequent offensive success while suppressing the opposing defense's hazard rate. The audit states this will drastically improve live in-play precision.

title: Replace folklore fractional Kelly kappa=0.25 with a bipolar inf-KL Kelly ceiling
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: The static, folklore-derived fractional Kelly criterion (kappa=0.25) in robust-kelly.ts is called a fundamental misunderstanding of portfolio sizing under Knightian uncertainty. Classical Kelly assumes the bettor knows the true distribution; when the model is misspecified, even a statically fractioned Kelly guarantees severe drawdowns. The fix is a bipolar Kelly ceiling based on inf-KL divergence: the optimal asymptotic growth rate under misspecification is set by the reverse information projection onto the bipolar enlargement of the model class, testing against all non-negative sequential tests (e-variables) that cannot distinguish the true distribution from the null.

title: E-process wealth accumulation with Ville's inequality for anytime-valid edge proof
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: An e-process is a non-negative stochastic process maintaining the supermartingale property under the null, representing the wealth of a sequential bettor. Formulating the test statistic as a sequential likelihood ratio (an e-value) invokes Ville's maximal inequality, bounding the probability of ever crossing threshold 1/alpha by alpha. The audit specifies forecast-skill-eprocess.ts continuously evaluating candidate models against market consensus, and that accumulated e-process wealth crossing 20 (for alpha=0.05) constitutes mathematically irrefutable evidence of edge regardless of when evaluation is halted or how often the data was peeked at. This formalizes the internal Baxley Causal E-Process Theory (CEPT) hypothesis as a deployable feature.

title: Longitudinal Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation for player-value causal effects
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: Standard regression and marginal replacement models for isolating player value or coaching acumen introduce severe confounding bias due to non-random NFL scheduling and substitution patterns. LTMLE is a doubly robust semi-parametric framework for dynamic treatment regimes with time-varying confounders: it estimates the conditional outcome mechanism (expected points added per play) alongside the treatment mechanism (probability a player or scheme is deployed given game state), generates Inverse Probability of Censoring Weights (IPCW), and applies a targeted fluctuation step solving the efficient influence curve equation. Using non-parametric Super Learner ensembles, the causal estimate is consistent if either model is correct.

title: Closed-form jump-diffusion safe-lead probability via the error function
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: Live in-play win probabilities should incorporate jump-diffusion mathematics. Modeling the score differential as a biased random walk yields an exact safe-lead probability erf(L / sqrt(4 D tau)), where L is the lead size, D is the diffusion coefficient representing scoring variance, and tau is remaining game time. The audit calls this a highly stable, computationally efficient closed-form baseline for the live predictive engine that anchors the more volatile ML outputs.

title: Murphy decomposition of the Brier score: reliability, resolution, uncertainty
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: The evaluation framework must natively compute the Murphy decomposition of the Brier score for all probabilistic outputs, partitioning it into Reliability, Resolution and Uncertainty. This matters most when judging market-anchored shrinkage (for example shrinking model probabilities toward the closing line by w=0.10): shrinkage artificially improves Reliability by mimicking the calibrated market while often decimating Resolution, the model's ability to distinguish distinct underlying risk states. If an update improves aggregate Brier solely through Reliability while degrading Resolution toward an uninformed prior, it is a loss of signal and must be rejected.

title: Clark-McCracken bootstrap test for nested model comparison
source_file: Algorithmic Audit_ Advancing Galaxy Sports Edge.pdf
summary: When a feature is added to an existing model, the asymptotic distribution of standard Diebold-Mariano statistics becomes non-standard because the forecast errors of the nested and nesting models are perfectly correlated under the null. The system must therefore implement the Clark-McCracken testing protocol using a bootstrap to estimate valid finite-sample critical values for nested out-of-sample forecast comparisons, preventing acceptance of false-positive improvements driven by parameter estimation noise.

title: Variance drag and first-passage objective distortion of Kelly utility

summary: The Kelly objective is expressed as E[log W_T] = integral of log w dF_T(w), whose logarithmic utility imposes an infinite penalty on zero wealth (ln 0 = -infinity), so an optimal Kelly strategy systematically avoids total capital loss. The document states this paradox makes sustained extreme daily targets mathematically unattainable.

title: Deep Hawkes Process for limit-order-book market making to capture the spread
source_file: Autonomous High-Leverage Algorithmic Trading Architecture_ Feasibility and Implementation for Small-Capital Accounts.docx
summary: A Deep Hawkes Process (DHP) models LOB dynamics as a self-exciting point process capturing temporal clustering: a burst of buy market orders raises the intensity of subsequent buy arrivals. Predicting order intensity lets the agent anticipate the next directional micro-trend and adjust quoting prices milliseconds before the wider market reacts, capturing the bid-ask spread instead of paying it.

title: PDT rule elimination in 2026 changes day-trade frequency constraints
source_file: Autonomous High-Leverage Algorithmic Trading Architecture_ Feasibility and Implementation for Small-Capital Accounts.docx
summary: On April 14, 2026 the SEC approved amendments to FINRA Rule 4210 eliminating the $25,000 minimum equity requirement and abolishing the pattern day trader classification entirely. title: Event-driven durable execution (Inngest) for autonomous 365-day operation
source_file: Autonomous High-Leverage Algorithmic Trading Architecture_ Feasibility and Implementation for Small-Capital Accounts.docx
summary: Traditional queue architectures (Redis, RabbitMQ, SQS) introduce failure points where a crashed process or serverless timeout loses state or duplicates executions. The blueprint instead relies on Inngest, an event-driven durable execution platform in Node.js/TypeScript, using durable functions invoked over HTTP. On failure from API rate limits, network latency or exchange downtime, Inngest retries from the exact failed step without restarting the sequence, providing at-least-once delivery while avoiding duplicate trade executions via transactional outbox patterns. Built-in concurrency limits, rate limiting and exponential backoff with jitter prevent overwhelming brokerage APIs.

title: Conformalized Quantile Regression with pinball loss for numeric lines

title: Quantile clamping must be banned; fail-closed refusal instead
source_file: World-Class Sports Probability Engine Corpus Audit.docx
summary: For a target miscoverage rate giving 90% coverage, the conformal rank index is ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)). With a small calibration sample the required rank index exceeds the available data, and because the empirical CDF cannot exceed 1.0 the quantile must evaluate to the maximum observed residual. Developers frequently apply a heuristic clamp to keep the system operational, but the audit proves this is mathematically catastrophic: selecting the maximum observed residual yields a true finite-sample coverage well below the nominal 90%, delivering a 6.67% under-coverage defect and deceptive fake tightness. The engine must explicitly ban clamping and instead enforce a strict fail-closed policy, emitting infinite intervals or abstaining via an automated No-Bet execution block.

title: Forecast-Skill E-process as a sequential likelihood-ratio martingale
source_file: World-Class Sports Probability Engine Corpus Audit.docx
summary: The LiveOrchestrator uses a Forecast-Skill E-process, an anytime-valid sequential likelihood-ratio martingale based on Ville's inequality. It tests the null hypothesis that the model's probabilities are no better than the market consensus. Because traditional p-values require fixed sample sizes and fail under continuous monitoring, the E-process lets the engine track compounded evidence of forecast skill continuously. If the martingale multiplies the theoretical capital it risks by a significant factor, it provides mathematically sound proof of predictive edge without absorbing-zero failures or p-hacking.

summary: The compound table builder computes qClose by devigging away and home moneylines into decimal odds and normalizing, and derives a spread-implied probability as 0.5*(1+erf((s/13.5)/sqrt(2))) where s is the spread line and 13.5 is the NFL standard deviation divisor. These two conversions are the bridge from market prices to model targets. The 13.5 divisor is an explicit NFL-specific constant that would need re-estimation for other sports.

title: CQR conformity score and quantile inflation
source_file: Auditing Conformal Prediction, Small-Sample Calibration, and Sports Market Probabilities for GSE.docx (Section A, CQR)
summary: Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR) fixes alpha_lo=alpha/2 and alpha_hi=1-alpha/2. Calibration conformity score E_i = max(q_alpha_lo(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_alpha_hi(X_i)). The interval is C(X) = [q_alpha_lo(X) - Q_1-alpha(E;I2), q_alpha_hi(X) + Q_1-alpha(E;I2)] where Q_1-alpha(E;I2) is the ceil((1-alpha)(|I2|+1))-th largest calibration score. Under exchangeability P{Y in C(X)} >= 1-alpha.

title: Jackknife+ interval for scarce calibration
source_file: Auditing Conformal Prediction, Small-Sample Calibration, and Sports Market Probabilities for GSE.docx (Section A, Jackknife+)
summary: Given leave-one-out fits mu_-i and residuals R_i^LOO = |Y_i - mu_-i(X_i)|, the jackknife+ interval is [q_alpha^-(mu_-i(Xn+1) - R_i^LOO), q_1-alpha^+(mu_-i(Xn+1) + R_i^LOO)]. title: Bradley-Terry-Luce MLE existence and uniqueness condition
source_file: Mathematical Verification and Architecture Audit_ Sports Rating Systems, Conformal Coverage, Football Analytics Schemas, Orchestration Durability, and Extraction Pipelines.docx (Section B2)
summary: MLE for the paired-comparison likelihood exists and is finite if and only if for every partition of entities into two non-empty sets, at least one entity in the first set defeated an entity in the second (strong connectivity of the comparison multigraph). An entity that wins all its contests drives its strength estimate to infinity; this divergence is an intrinsic property of the unregularized logistic likelihood supremum, not an algorithmic fault. Any rating fitter in GSE must therefore detect perfect separation and fail closed or regularize rather than returning a large finite number.

title: Newman spectral Bradley-Terry normalization: geometric mean to 1

title: Zermelo and spectral BT fixed-point update equations
source_file: Mathematical Verification and Architecture Audit_ Sports Rating Systems, Conformal Coverage, Football Analytics Schemas, Orchestration Durability, and Extraction Pipelines.docx (Section B2-B3, Eqs 3,4,9,12)
summary: Zermelo fixed point: pi'_i = sum_j w_ij / sum_j (w_ij + w_ji)/(pi_i + pi_j). Spectral/off-diagonal variant: pi'_i = [sum_j w_ij pi_j/(pi_i + pi_j)] / [sum_j w_ji/(pi_i + pi_j)]. Both must return null when any pi_k <= 0, when a denominator term pi_i + pi_j = 0, when total matches w_ij + w_ji = 0 for all j, or for an undefeated node (denominator zero). Convergence is not guaranteed on bipartite or nearly disconnected comparison graphs without damping.

title: BT log-likelihood and score equations (Eqs 5,6,7)
source_file: Mathematical Verification and Architecture Audit_ Sports Rating Systems, Conformal Coverage, Football Analytics Schemas, Orchestration Durability, and Extraction Pipelines.docx (Section B2, arXiv:2207.00076)
summary: Log-likelihood L(pi) = prod_{i<j} (pi_i/(pi_i+pi_j))^{w_ij} (pi_j/(pi_i+pi_j))^{w_ji}; log form ell(pi) = sum_{i,j} [w_ij ln pi_i - w_ij ln(pi_i + pi_j)]. Score equation: d(ell)/d(pi_i) = (sum_j w_ij)/pi_i - sum_j (w_ij + w_ji)/(pi_i + pi_j) = 0. Scale is unidentifiable without a gauge-fixing constraint (prod pi_i = 1 or pi_1 = 1), and roots do not yield finite MLEs under perfect separation.

title: Plackett-Luce stagewise extension for multi-way rankings
source_file: Mathematical Verification and Architecture Audit_ Sports Rating Systems, Conformal Coverage, Football Analytics Schemas, Orchestration Durability, and Extraction Pipelines.docx (Section B2, arXiv:2601.14727v2, Extension PL)

title: Thurstone-Mosteller probit vs Bradley-Terry logistic dispersion
source_file: Mathematical Verification and Architecture Audit_ Sports Rating Systems, Conformal Coverage, Football Analytics Schemas, Orchestration Durability, and Extraction Pipelines.docx (Section B4, arXiv:2406.09597)
summary: Probit link: P(i > j) = Phi((mu_i - mu_j)/sqrt(sigma_i^2 + sigma_j^2)); logistic link: P(i > j) = 1/(1 + exp(-(lambda_i - lambda_j))). Thurstone-Mosteller assumes latent normal dispersion while BT assumes Gumbel dispersion, giving a standard logistic distribution for utility differences; the two links do not give identical closed-form odds ratios. Home advantage requires an explicit shift parameter alpha inside the difference.

title: Strictly proper scoring rule decomposition: entropy, exposure, penalty
source_file: Mathematical Verification and Architecture Audit_ Sports Rating Systems, Conformal Coverage, Football Analytics Schemas, Orchestration Durability, and Extraction Pipelines.docx (arXiv:2509.08744v1, Table 2)
summary: Every scoring rule decomposes into three geometric components. Brier: entropy = p(p-1), exposure = 2p, penalty = 1. Log: entropy = p*ln(p) + (1-p)*ln(1-p), exposure = ln(p/(1-p)), penalty = 1/(p(1-p)) with essential poles at p=0 and p=1. Spherical: entropy = -sqrt(p^2+(1-p)^2), exposure = p/sqrt(p^2+(1-p)^2), penalty = 1/(p^2+(1-p)^2)^(3/2).

title: ZFC undecidability: theorem set is recursively enumerable not recursive
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (zfc_undecidability)
summary: Thm_ZFC is in Sigma_1^0 minus Delta_1^0: the set of theorems of an effectively axiomatized formal system is recursively enumerable and not recursive (Church-Turing undecidability of first-order logic; Post's theorem). Non-claim: proof checking is primitive recursive and remains decidable.

title: Dedup normalization hierarchy: decode, fold newlines, banner strip only
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (Shingling, MinHash, SimHash)
summary: Document deduplication requires normalization before any hash: (1) byte decoding to standard Unicode, (2) newline folding \r\n to \n, (3) stripping trailing institutional banners ONLY when an unambiguous banner grammar is specified. Removing inline TeX comments, macro definitions or mathematical exponents is prohibited because it can eliminate errata corrections, macro definitions and operational terms. Exact SHA-256 over raw files collapses worktree copies but fails on documents differing only by newline formatting.

title: Broder resemblance r_w(A,B) over w-shingles
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (broder_resemblance)
summary: r_w(A,B) = |S(A,w) intersect S(B,w)| / |S(A,w) union S(B,w)|, the Jaccard resemblance of the w-shingle sets of documents A and B (Broder 1997, page 22). title: Broder containment c_w(A,B) and its asymmetry trap
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (broder_containment)
summary: c_w(A,B) = |S(A,w) intersect S(B,w)| / |S(A,w)|, the containment of A in B (Broder 1997, page 22). Null if |S(A,w)| = 0. Non-claim: containment is not symmetric, c_w(A,B) != c_w(B,A) in general. Using containment as a merge rule false-merges a macro library into every paper importing it; using it as an inclusion filter rejects short math notes embedded in larger reviews.

title: Broder min-s sketch resemblance estimator

title: MinHash false-merge: shared preamble P dominates resemblance
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (MinHash false-merges)
summary: With A = P union M1 and B = P union M2 where M1 intersect M2 is empty, exact Jaccard resemblance is r(A,B) = |P| / (|P| + |M1| + |M2|). Case A: |P| = 400 and |M1| = |M2| = 50 merges two mathematically disjoint documents at a typical operational threshold. Case B: |P| = 2,000 and |M1| = |M2| = 500 also merges them despite 500 unique lines of substantive math each. Case C containment trap: an isolated 200-line macro package against a 5,000-line paper importing it yields containment near 1.

title: False-split failure mode: erratum exponent correction near resemblance 1
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (False-split failure mode)
summary: If document E is an erratum correcting a single exponent in paper A, shingle-level document resemblance between E and A stays near unity (approximately 1), indicating identical papers, while an isolated math-span hash splits the equations and records them as distinct formulas. Merging solely on document resemblance false-merges contradictory formulas; splitting solely on cryptographic equation hashes false-splits the underlying papers. Neither signal alone is sufficient.

title: LSH banding false-merge probability 1 - (1 - s^r)^b
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (LSH banding)
summary: For b bands of r rows each, the probability that two documents with resemblance s become candidate pairs is 1 - (1 - s^r)^b. A configuration of b bands and r rows flags documents sharing only generic introductions (low s) as duplicates with high probability. Applying a single global threshold across heterogeneous corpora causes web pages sharing navigation elements to collapse into identical clusters.

title: Dedup arbitration: withhold merge when MinHash and SimHash disagree
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (SimHash vs MinHash arbitration)
summary: Operational rules stated: if MinHash and SimHash yield contradictory candidate decisions, merging is withheld. Math-span hashing is performed downstream of syntax validation, so truncated spans and malformed expressions are rejected prior to index insertion. Dense embedding models serve strictly to re-rank pre-filtered candidate clusters; relying on embedding cosine thresholds alone risks merging distinct derivations that share generic narrative commentary.

title: Glicko-2 volatility root equation and Illinois iteration
source_file: Formal Verification, Deduplication Bounds, and Execution Routing Architecture for Algorithmic Rating and Inference Systems.docx (glicko2_volatility_root, Step 5)
summary: f(x) = e^x (Delta^2 - phi^2 - v - e^x) / (2 (phi^2 + v + e^x)^2) - (x - ln(sigma^2)) / tau^2, where x = ln(sigma'^2) and tau in [0.3, 1.2]. Procedure: set convergence tolerance epsilon = 1e-6, find bracket [A, B], apply the Illinois algorithm to locate root x*, then sigma' = e^(x*/2). Null if Illinois fails to converge within 100 steps or yields non-finite volatility. Non-claim: arbitrary updates are not permitted without executing the bracketed root search.

title: Banister two-component fitness-fatigue impulse-response model
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 451-520)
summary: Athlete performance is modeled as a two-component exponential impulse response: p_t = p_0 + k1 * sum_{i=1}^{t-1} w_i * exp(-(t-i)/tau_1) - k2 * sum_{i=1}^{t-1} w_i * exp(-(t-i)/tau_2), where w_i is training load at session i, tau_1 is the fitness decay constant (45 days) and tau_2 the fatigue decay constant (11 days). Fitness accumulates slowly and fatigue decays quickly, so net readiness is fitness minus fatigue. The model supplies a physiological prior for minutes and usage projections rather than a direct win probability.

title: Zero step score nullifies the cumulative trajectory product and prunes the reasoning branch
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 170-230)

title: Backward error correction for noisy verifiers: R_backward = (R_tilde - rho_0) / (1 - rho_0 - rho_1)
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 172-224)
summary: Following Cai et al. (2025), the verifier is modeled as a binary stochastic channel mapping true latent validity R_star in {0,1} to observed feedback R_tilde in {0,1}, with false positive rate rho_0 = P(R_tilde = 1 | R_star = 0) and false negative rate rho_1 = P(R_tilde = 0 | R_star = 1). The engine constructs an unbiased surrogate reward by backward error correction: R_backward = (R_tilde - rho_0) / (1 - rho_0 - rho_1). If the verifier becomes uninformative, that is when 1 - rho_0 - rho_1 <= 0, execution halts immediately to prevent policy corruption.

title: Split conformal non-conformity quantile with finite-sample correction
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 225-280)
summary: The engine integrates split conformal prediction over a calibration set of n exchangeable historical events (X_i, Y_i) with non-conformity scores s_i = |Y_i - mu_hat(X_i)|. The quantile threshold is defined as q_hat = inf{ q : (1/n) * sum_{i=1}^{n} I(s_i <= q) >= ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha))/n }, which yields marginal coverage P(Y_{n+1} in C(X_{n+1})) >= 1 - alpha. The ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)) term is the finite-sample correction that keeps coverage valid for small n.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference under non-exchangeability: alpha_(t+1) = alpha_t + gamma*(alpha - err_t)
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 280-303)
summary: Because athletic competitions exhibit distribution drift across seasons and tactical shifts, exchangeability is frequently violated, so the engine deploys Adaptive Conformal Inference and updates the rolling miscoverage level with alpha_(t+1) = alpha_t + gamma*(alpha - err_t), where err_t = I{Y_t not in C_t} and gamma is the learning rate. This tracks time-varying coverage instead of assuming a stationary exchangeable sequence. It is the bridge between the static split-conformal guarantee and live drift.

The bounds give a parameter-free sanity check that does not depend on the chosen copula family.

title: Clayton copula for lower-tail clustering with closed-form tail dependence 2^(-1/theta)
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 389-418)
summary: Correlations in athletic contests are asymmetric, so the engine pairs symmetric Frank copulas with Clayton and Gumbel families. The Clayton copula is C_theta(u_1,u_2) = (u_1^(-theta) + u_2^(-theta) - 1)^(-1/theta) with lower-tail dependence lambda_L = 2^(-1/theta) and upper-tail dependence lambda_U = 0, appropriate for defensive slugfests where outcomes cluster in the lower tail. The closed forms make tail dependence directly computable from the fitted parameter.

title: Gumbel copula for upper-tail clustering with lambda_U = 2 - 2^(1/theta)
source_file: Comprehensive Architecture Audit_ Multi-Agent Fleet Orchestration.docx (lines 418-449)
summary: The Gumbel copula is C_theta(u_1,u_2) = exp( -[ (-ln u_1)^theta + (-ln u_2)^theta ]^(1/theta) ) with upper-tail dependence lambda_U = 2 - 2^(1/theta) and lambda_L = 0, matching high-scoring overtime shootouts where outcomes cluster in the upper tail. Fitting only a Frank copula would impose symmetric dependence and miss this asymmetry. The lambda_U formula gives an immediate diagnostic of how strongly legs co-move in the tail.
